AGREEMENT AND PLAN OF MERGER
by and among
COBALT ANALYTICS, INC.
NORTHWIND HOLDINGS, INC.
NORTHWIND MERGER SUB I, INC.
and
FORTIS SHAREHOLDER REPRESENTATIVE, LLC (solely as the Stockholder Representative)
Dated as of May 20, 2025

RECITALS
WHEREAS, Northwind Holdings, Inc. ("Parent") desires to acquire Cobalt Analytics, Inc. ("Company") through the merger (the "Merger") of Northwind Merger Sub I, Inc. ("Merger Sub"), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Parent, with and into the Company, with the Company surviving.

ARTICLE I — THE MERGER
1.1 The Merger. At the Effective Time, Merger Sub shall be merged with and into the Company in accordance with Section 251 of the DGCL. The Company shall be the surviving corporation.
1.2 Merger Consideration. The aggregate consideration payable to the Company's stockholders (the "Merger Consideration") shall be $46,500,000 in cash, subject to adjustment for (i) Net Working Capital, (ii) Cash and Cash Equivalents, (iii) Indebtedness, and (iv) Transaction Expenses, in each case as of the Closing.
1.3 Escrow. $4,650,000 of the Merger Consideration (10%) shall be held in escrow with Northern Trust for 18 months following the Closing as security for the Company's indemnification obligations.
1.4 Company Equity Awards. Vested Company Options shall be cashed out at the Closing at a per-share price equal to (Merger Consideration ÷ fully-diluted share count) minus the exercise price. Unvested awards shall be terminated at the Effective Time.

ARTICLE II — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF THE COMPANY
2.1 Corporate Existence. The Company is a corporation duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of Delaware.
2.2 Capitalization. Section 2.2 of the Disclosure Schedule sets forth the authorized and outstanding capital stock of the Company. Except as disclosed, there are no outstanding options, warrants, or other rights to acquire capital stock of the Company.
2.3 Financial Statements. The Company has delivered to Parent the audited financial statements for FY2023 and FY2024 (the "Financial Statements"), which present fairly in all material respects the financial condition of the Company.
2.4 Absence of Undisclosed Liabilities. Except as set forth in Section 2.4 of the Disclosure Schedule, the Company has no liabilities that would be required to be reflected on a balance sheet prepared in accordance with GAAP.
2.5 Material Contracts. Section 2.5 of the Disclosure Schedule lists each Material Contract.
2.6 Litigation. Except as set forth in Section 2.6 of the Disclosure Schedule, there is no action, suit, or proceeding pending or, to the Company's Knowledge, threatened against the Company.
2.7 Intellectual Property. Section 2.7 of the Disclosure Schedule sets forth all registered Intellectual Property of the Company.
2.8 Employees and ERISA. Section 2.8 of the Disclosure Schedule sets forth all Employee Benefit Plans.
2.9 Tax Matters. All required Tax Returns have been timely filed and all Taxes shown as due have been paid.

ARTICLE III — COVENANTS
3.1 Conduct of Business. From the date hereof until Closing, the Company shall operate in the ordinary course consistent with past practice.
3.2 No-Shop. During the pre-closing period, the Company shall not solicit, initiate, or engage in discussions concerning any Alternative Transaction. If the Company terminates this Agreement to accept a Superior Proposal, the Company shall pay Parent a termination fee of $1,860,000 (4%).
3.3 Regulatory Filings. The parties shall use reasonable best efforts to obtain all required regulatory approvals, including any required HSR Act filings.

ARTICLE IV — INDEMNIFICATION
4.1 Survival. The representations and warranties shall survive for 18 months, except for Fundamental Representations (24 months) and Tax representations (until the applicable statute of limitations).
4.2 Basket and Cap. The Company shall not be liable for indemnification claims until the aggregate amount of Losses exceeds $232,500 (0.5%), after which the Company shall be liable for all Losses in excess of that amount. Total indemnification is capped at the Escrow Amount ($4,650,000) except for Fundamental Reps and Fraud, which are uncapped.

ARTICLE V — CONDITIONS TO CLOSING
5.1 Stockholder Approval. The Merger requires the affirmative vote of holders of a majority of the outstanding Company Common Stock in accordance with DGCL § 251(c).
5.2 Regulatory. Any required HSR Act waiting period shall have expired.
5.3 No MAC. There shall not have occurred any Material Adverse Change since the date of this Agreement.
5.4 Third-Party Consents. The consents set forth on Section 5.4 of the Disclosure Schedule shall have been obtained.

ARTICLE VI — GOVERNING LAW; JURISDICTION
This Agreement is governed by the laws of Delaware. The parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the date first written above.
